grammar.title: 有沒有 — asking if something exists
grammar.explanation: To ask whether something exists or is available, put 有沒有 ("have-not-have") before the noun. It's a quick yes/no question that doesn't need 嗎.

grammar.title: 了 — a completed action
grammar.explanation: 了 after the verb marks that the action happened / is done: 買了 = bought. It's one of the most common uses of 了 in everyday Taiwan speech.

grammar.title: Time before the verb
grammar.explanation: In Chinese the time when something happens comes before the verb, not after: 我晚上回家 = I go home in the evening. Time can also lead the whole sentence.

He has to work in the afternoon.

grammar.title: 往 — moving toward a direction
grammar.explanation: 往 (wǎng) marks the direction of movement and comes before the verb: 往前走 = walk forward, 往右轉 = turn right.

grammar.title: 用 — the means / instrument
grammar.explanation: 用 ("to use") marks the tool or method you do something with. Put 用 + the means before the verb: 用現金付 = pay with cash.

grammar.title: 只 — only
grammar.explanation: 只 ("only") goes right before the verb to limit it: 只收現金 = only accept cash.
